title.rendered: Signs Will Accompany Those Who Believe: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: These signs will accompany those who believe: they will drive out demons, speak in new tongues, place their hands on sick people, and they will get well. Signs accompany the believer, not just the specialist.

content.rendered:
These signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up snakes with their hands; and when they drink deadly poison, it will not hurt them at all; they will place their hands on sick people, and they will get well. Signs accompany the believer, not just the specialist. The New Testament expects the miraculous to follow every Christian who walks in the name.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, July 24, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And these signs will accompany those who believe: In my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up snakes with their hands; and when they drink deadly poison, it will not hurt them at all; they will place their hands on sick people, and they will get well.”
Mark 16:17-18 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Mark closes his Gospel with the risen Jesus commissioning His followers to preach the good news to all creation. The Great Commission in Mark’s version is followed immediately by a list of the signs that will accompany believers as they carry the gospel forward. Read the list carefully. Jesus did not say these signs will accompany the apostles. He did not say they will accompany specially anointed evangelists. He said they will accompany those who believe. All who believe. The signs are part of the standard equipment of the ordinary believer walking in the name of Jesus.

The signs Jesus names span the categories of authority the New Testament associates with the believer’s ministry. Driving out demons. Deliverance ministry. Speaking in new tongues. The gift of the Spirit that came at Pentecost and remains available today. Protection from harm, whether from serpents or poison, the picture Luke would later illustrate in Paul’s shipwreck on Malta in Acts 28. And the laying on of hands for the healing of the sick. Every one of these signs is documented across the Book of Acts and the wider New Testament as part of the normal experience of the early church.

What has changed over the intervening two thousand years is not the promise. It is the expectation. Many believers today have been taught that these signs belonged to a special era, that they were needed to authenticate the apostolic ministry and have since ceased. That teaching is a matter of theological interpretation Christians debate in good faith. What is undeniable, however, is what Jesus actually said. He said the signs will accompany those who believe. He did not append an expiration date. He did not restrict the list to a first-century audience. He described the ordinary ministry of Christians walking in His name after His ascension.

For Gospelbuzz readers whose churches trace their heritage through the great missionary movements to Africa, the Caribbean, Southeast Asia and Latin America, the signs Jesus named are not theoretical. Deliverance still happens. Healing still happens. The Spirit still fills. In many of the most vital churches of the global south, in fact, the signs Jesus named are the daily fabric of ministry. The believer walking in the name of Jesus should not be surprised when the promised signs follow. The Lord who spoke them has not changed His mind.

The right posture is not presumption. It is not demanding signs on demand. It is faith, expectant, quiet, humble, and available. When the believer walks with Christ and speaks in His name, the Spirit sovereignly moves. Sometimes in visible signs. Sometimes in hidden work. Always in ways that glorify Jesus. Walk in that expectant faith today. The Christ who spoke the signs still confirms His Word with what follows.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have promised signs to accompany those who believe in the name of Jesus. I walk in that name today. I am available for whatever You choose to do through me. If deliverance is needed, I am willing. If healing is needed, I am willing. If the Spirit chooses to fill and move, I am willing. I do not demand signs. I walk in humble, expectant faith, trusting that the Christ who spoke these promises is faithful to confirm His Word. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Signs accompany those who believe in the name of Jesus. I walk in that name today. The Christ who spoke the promises is faithful to confirm His Word.
